comments.body: 2026-10-25: there are 8 of them, not 2: pids 52348 52421 52454 52456 52576 52611 52778 52789, all started 2026-10-03 from ~/src/muster-1/target/debug (sockets d37529-187/188/193/204 and d37712-187/188/193/203), each about 16 MB footprint plus a pane shell, about 26,900 CPU-seconds between them over 22 days. Quartermaster now raises them as an orphan alert ('16 processes running from muster's directory have run for 22 days 1 hour with no agent session or job attached'). muster daemons does not list them, since test daemons are not written under ~/.muster/state/daemons.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Filed by Quartermaster's orchestrator (an agent), not the owner: its attribution spike found these while sampling the Mac on 2026-10-17, and they are left untouched.

Two debug `muster-daemon`s started on 2026-10-03 10:59 from the muster-1 worktree are still alive 14 days later, reparented to launchd: pids 52348 and 52454, `~/src/muster-1/target/debug/muster-daemon --socket /tmp/muster-test/d37529-187/daemon.sock` and `.../d37712-187/daemon.sock`, `--data .../crates/muster-harness/../../deps/...`. Each holds one pane shell (`/bin/sh -l -i -c ... command eval "$MUSTER_PANE_COMMAND"`, pids 52364 and 52463) that starts a `sleep 1` every second: about 1,100 processes in 10 minutes between them, little CPU, but process churn every sampler on the Mac has to read. The `/tmp/muster-test/dNNNNN-187` socket names suggest a harness run whose test process died (or was killed) before its daemons were stopped, so nothing reaped them.

Worth a look: whether muster-harness ties each daemon's life to the test process (a pipe the daemon watches, or a process group the harness kills on drop and on a panic), and whether `./dev --doctor` lists strays like these. Quartermaster has not signalled them; ending them is the owner's or muster's call.
title: 🧟 Harness test daemons from 3 Oct still running, each pane shell looping sleep 1
